enonce_intro_markdown:
A particle $P$ of unit mass is moving on a horizontal plane under the action of a force $\mathbf{F}$ at time $t$ seconds, where

$$\mathbf{F} = \left[(3t^2 - 4t)\,\mathbf{i} + (6t - 5)\,\mathbf{j}\right]\ \mathrm{N}$$

Given that $P$ passes through a point $A$ with velocity $(11\mathbf{i} + 10\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ after 3 seconds,

find

questions.enonce_markdown: the acceleration of $P$ at time $t$ seconds,
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** $P$ has mass $m = 1\ \mathrm{kg}$ and moves in the horizontal plane, with the unit vectors $\mathbf{i}$, $\mathbf{j}$ along the two axes. The force $\mathbf{F}$ given is the resultant force on $P$, so Newton's second law $\mathbf{F} = m\mathbf{a}$ applies component by component.

$$\mathbf{a} = \frac{\mathbf{F}}{m} = \frac{\mathbf{F}}{1}$$

**The acceleration of $P$ at time $t$ is**

$$\mathbf{a} = \left[(3t^2 - 4t)\,\mathbf{i} + (6t - 5)\,\mathbf{j}\right]\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}.$$

questions.enonce_markdown: the velocity of $P$ at time $t$ seconds,
questions.corrige_markdown:
Velocity is the integral of acceleration with respect to time, so integrate each component and add a constant vector $c_1\mathbf{i} + c_2\mathbf{j}$:

$$\mathbf{v} = \int \mathbf{a}\,dt = \left(t^3 - 2t^2 + c_1\right)\mathbf{i} + \left(3t^2 - 5t + c_2\right)\mathbf{j}$$

Use the condition $\mathbf{v} = 11\mathbf{i} + 10\mathbf{j}$ when $t = 3$:

- $\mathbf{i}$ component: $27 - 18 + c_1 = 11 \;\Rightarrow\; c_1 = 2$;
- $\mathbf{j}$ component: $27 - 15 + c_2 = 10 \;\Rightarrow\; c_2 = -2$.

**The velocity of $P$ at time $t$ is**

$$\mathbf{v} = \left[(t^3 - 2t^2 + 2)\,\mathbf{i} + (3t^2 - 5t - 2)\,\mathbf{j}\right]\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.$$

(Check at $t = 3$: $27 - 18 + 2 = 11$ and $27 - 15 - 2 = 10$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: the kinetic energy of $P$ when it is moving parallel to the vector $\mathbf{i}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
$P$ moves parallel to $\mathbf{i}$ when its $\mathbf{j}$ component of velocity is zero (and its $\mathbf{i}$ component is not):

$$3t^2 - 5t - 2 = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; (3t + 1)(t - 2) = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; t = 2 \ \text{ or } \ t = -\tfrac13.$$

Time is measured forwards from the start of the motion, so $t \ge 0$ and $t = 2\ \mathrm{s}$ (the root $t = -\tfrac13$ is rejected).

At $t = 2$: $\mathbf{v} = (8 - 8 + 2)\,\mathbf{i} + 0\,\mathbf{j} = 2\mathbf{i}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The $\mathbf{i}$ component is non-zero, so $P$ is really moving parallel to $\mathbf{i}$, with speed $2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

Kinetic energy, with $m = 1\ \mathrm{kg}$:

$$\mathrm{KE} = \tfrac12 m v^2 = \tfrac12 \times 1 \times 2^2 = 2\ \mathrm{J}.$$

**The kinetic energy of $P$ is $2\ \mathrm{J}$** (at $t = 2\ \mathrm{s}$).

questions.enonce_markdown: Another particle $Q$ moves in the same straight path as $P$ with velocity $(3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Determine the velocity of $P$ relative to $Q$ at time $t = 2$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The velocity of $P$ relative to $Q$ is $\mathbf{v}_{PQ} = \mathbf{v}_P - \mathbf{v}_Q$.

At $t = 2$, from part (b) (or part (c)), $\mathbf{v}_P = 2\mathbf{i}$, and $\mathbf{v}_Q = 3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j}$ (given):

$$\mathbf{v}_{PQ} = (2\mathbf{i}) - (3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j}) = -\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j}.$$

**The velocity of $P$ relative to $Q$ at $t = 2$ is $(-\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$**, of magnitude $\sqrt{1 + 16} = \sqrt{17} \approx 4.12\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.
